objections.claim: The design closes every run through one guard, but the sentry-abort exit is precisely the case where an admitted issue is *deliberately* left without a terminal outcome — `applySentryAbort` "NEVER writes outcomes — the in-flight issue stays undispatched so the run is re-enterable". On that exit, `close` step 2 always refuses (exit 3), and the spec's only routing is "step 11's 'dispatch or park' for `undispatched`, then close again". But a sentry-aborted run must not dispatch ("no further builds launch", SKILL l. 639), so the only way to satisfy the guard is to park the in-flight issue — which converts a resumable abort into terminal parks. The alternative — the skill simply never reaching a successful `close` — means no `stop_reason`, no owner close, no `run-end` event, no judge-trail for one of the six documented stop conditions, violating the run-end synchronicity invariant the spec itself carries at l. 385. The builder cannot fix this in the build: the guard's position and the refusal semantics are spec'd, and the spec explicitly rules out a terminal bucket (§2) without noticing that the aborted path is where one is structurally needed.
objections.evidence: spec §4.2 step 2 and the edge case "An aborted run with undispatched admitted issues. `close` refuses (exit 3) exactly as `runcheck` and its Stop hook already do today"; `bin/lib/sentry.js` l. 883–886 ("the in-flight issue stays undispatched so the run is re-enterable"); `bin/lib/resume.js` l. 43 (aborted-resumable is the first re-enterable state); SKILL l. 639 (sentry-abort is a run-level stop). Note the spec's own C33 rationale ("`aborted-resumable` owner kept at close") only addresses the owner-status write in close step 4 — which is unreachable on this path because step 2 refused first.
objections.predicted_consequence: every real sentry abort ends with either (a) the in-flight issue force-parked, so `faff resume` finds no `aborted-resumable` work to re-enter and the abort's resumability guarantee is silently destroyed, or (b) the run-end bracket never runs and the ledger is left without `stop_reason`/`owner` close — the exact abandoned-run failure FAFF-1437 exists to mechanise.
objections.disposition_rationale: Abort exemption: a sentry-abort close of a run carrying the abort mark closes, reports undispatched, leaves outcomes untouched.

objections.claim: Prose runs `hooks-ensure` "on first autonomous run" unconditionally (l. 450); the spec moves it into `open` step 6 but orders governance ahead of it, so on the exit-3 fail-closed path — plausibly a repo's *first* autonomous run, since an unconfigured/misconfigured governor is exactly a first-run condition — hooks are never ensured, while §4.3 deletes the standalone `hooks-ensure` block from the skill. A first run that fail-closes leaves the Stop-hook backstop unregistered with no remaining call site.
objections.evidence: spec §4.1 step 7 FAIL_CLOSED ("Steps 5 and 6 never run"); §4.3 "Stop hook (l. 450–457): the `hooks-ensure` code block goes".
objections.predicted_consequence: on a fail-closed first run, `runcheck --hook` and `prepcheck --hook` are not registered; the hook backstop is absent for that session's subsequent runs.
objections.disposition_rationale: hooks-ensure now runs on both the success and fail-closed paths.

objections.claim: `run open --adopt-run-dir` accepts any directory containing a parseable `run-ledger.json` and proceeds through enrich, governance, poller start and exit 0 with no check that the adopted run is not already **live-held by a concurrent session**, not `done-clean`, and not `aborted-resumable`-pending-resume. The concurrent-session threat model is not hypothetical here: the ledger's whole owner/heartbeat apparatus exists precisely because "a parallel session's hook can't distinguish 'an orchestrator is actively draining this' from 'this queue was deferred'", and `faff resume` enforces exactly this via `classifyReEnterable` (refusing `live-running` and `done-clean`, ledger untouched, exit 2). The spec's adopt path bypasses that classification entirely: a second session (or a second orchestrator turn in the same repo) can adopt a run whose heartbeat sidecar is fresh, start a second sentry-poller, pass governance as `already-governed` under the *same* producer identity, and begin dispatching builds against a run another driver is actively draining — interleaved event appends, two pollers, two build lanes on one `admitted` list. Note there is no per-session ownership field to fall back on: the prose itself records `owner.session_id` as the run-id, so the heartbeat-held bit is the *only* live-driver signal, and the spec's step 1 validation stops at "must parse to an object".
objections.evidence: §4.1 step 1 — "IF --adopt-run-dir: run_dir := it; its run-ledger.json must parse to an object, else exit 2" — is the sole adopt validation; §4.4 "Re-running `open --adopt-run-dir`" considers only the re-open/envelope case, never the live-held case; context `resume.js` l.40–51 defines the refusal states the verb never consults; SKILL.md l.420 states the concurrent-session threat the design otherwise guards.
objections.predicted_consequence: two concurrent drivers drain one run under one Commissaire producer identity; the second driver's dispatches and event appends interleave with the first's, and the run's completeness/governance evidence chain is written by two unsynchronised writers.
objections.disposition_rationale: --adopt-run-dir adopts only a running run whose $FAFF_RUN_DIR names it.

objections.claim: the prose runs `effect reconcile` + `verdict conclude` only "for each issue admitted on **a governed run**" — knowledge settled at open time. The spec replaces that with a fresh close-time status probe and, on probe failure/timeout/unparseable output, flips to the governed branch and runs the conclude loop anyway. This rests on the unverified assertion that conclude on an ungoverned run "fails harmlessly" — a claim about an unchanged Commissaire subsystem the spec does not evidence. If conclude's ungoverned-run behaviour is not a clean non-zero no-write (e.g. it records an unanchored/unsigned verdict row), the spec has built a fail-open path: a governance probe outage causes governance-grade verdict writes on a run that was never admitted. The safe direction is the prose's own: carry open-time governance forward, or on probe failure skip (fail toward "no governance write"), never run governance writes on an unverified run.
objections.evidence: §4.2 step 6 — "IF probe.governed === true, OR the probe failed, timed out or was unparseable: … conclude loop"; Chosen rationale asserts only that "on an ungoverned run, `effect reconcile` and `verdict conclude` fail harmlessly and are logged"; prose l.441 gates on governed-run membership, not a fresh probe.
objections.predicted_consequence: a Commissaire outage at close time turns into conclude calls against an ungoverned run; harmless only if Commissaire's ungoverned conclude is verified no-write — which the spec asserts but no test pins (the test list covers "a failed status probe still running the loop" on a governed ledger, not on an ungoverned one).
objections.disposition_rationale: The probe-failure-as-governed conclude loop cites cmdReconcile (read-only) and cmdTerminalVerdict (no write unless admitted), with a test.

objections.claim: The second holdout scenario's final `Then` asserts a negative — "no sentry-poller handle exists for the run" — but the spec never states where or in what form a started poller leaves an observable handle (pid file, ledger key, state dir). A code-blind holdout evaluator, and a tester running the scenario cold, cannot decide this without inventing the observation method, and a builder could satisfy or fail it depending on which handle representation they assume.
objections.evidence: Holdout scenario "Given a repo whose config sets commissaire.governor to an endpoint nothing listens on … And … no sentry-poller handle exists for the run".
objections.predicted_consequence: The holdout verdict for this scenario is undecidable as written; two correct builds could be judged differently on the same assertion.
objections.disposition_rationale: The holdout's poller assertion uses faff sentry-poller status --json.

objections.claim: `open` step 5 (and FAIL_CLOSED) spawn `faff hooks-ensure --root`, but the prose (C16, l. 450–457) and every context excerpt show `hooks-ensure` invoked bare with no flags; nothing in the supplied context establishes that the verb accepts `--root`. The spec hard-codes the flag into both the success and fail-closed paths.
objections.evidence: spec §4.1 step 5 / FAIL_CLOSED ("Spawn `faff hooks-ensure --root`"); SKILL.md l. 452–455 runs `"$faff" hooks-ensure` with no arguments.
objections.predicted_consequence: if the verb does not take `--root`, every open (including every fail-closed open) records `steps.hooks: "failed:<exit>"` with `hooks_report: null` while still exiting 0 — the skill relays nothing (C17) and the Stop-hook backstop is never registered, yet the DONE item "run open runs it" reads as satisfied. A one-line spec edit (drop the flag, or state that `hooks-ensure` gains it) removes the risk.
objections.disposition_rationale: hooks-ensure --root is the verb's existing flag: usage: faff hooks-ensure [--root DIR] [--local] [--dry-run] [--json].

objections.claim: `close` step 4 rewrites `stop_reason := token` unconditionally on every pass, and §4.4's "close twice" edge case assumes "the second call re-writes the same `stop_reason`" — but nothing enforces sameness. A run closed once with an escalate-class token (`non-convergence`, `sentry-abort`, `governance-admit-failed`, `budget-escalated(...)`) can be closed again with a quiet token (e.g. `queue-drained`), and the escalate-class value that `faff disposition` keys on — the durable signal a human sees after the container dies — is silently replaced in the same locked edit that re-stamps `owner.status:"done"`. The prose (l. 440) writes `stop_reason` once at the real exit; the verb makes it a rewritable field with no guard, and the refusal path (step 2) does not run because a fail-closed or escalated run can easily have zero undispatched issues (all parked). This is the failure-as-bypass shape: the second close is an error path that silently removes a check the first close established.
objections.evidence: §4.2 step 4 ("Locked edit, one write: stop_reason := token; owner.status := 'done'…"); §4.4 "close twice" ("The second call re-writes the same `stop_reason`… a second `run-end` event is appended"); §3 Stop tokens lists `governance-admit-failed` "so a re-close of a fail-closed run validates" — i.e. re-close is an anticipated path, yet no idempotence-or-refuse rule is stated for a differing token; `disposition.js` (`isEscalateStopReason`) reads only `ledger.stop_reason`.
objections.predicted_consequence: `faff disposition` classifies the run as a configured quiet stop and raises no run-escalation item; a run that ended in `non-convergence` or a sentry abort pages nobody, with the ledger showing a clean drain.
objections.spec_anchor: 42-run-close (the `PROCEDURE run_close` block; attackable edit is step 4) — under `### 4.2 \`run close\``.
objections.disposition_rationale: A re-close with a different token exits 2 and writes nothing; the same token is idempotent.

objections.claim: A tester cannot state the expected `OpenResult`/`CloseResult` JSON for the failure exits. §3 says `owner_status: ENUM done | aborted-resumable | null` without saying *when* it is null; likewise `run_dir` / `fail_closed_cause` / `budget_envelope` on exit 2 (refused adopt, malformed `--until`, post-mint write failure) and on a `close` exit-3 refusal. The DONE item "`--json` prints an OpenResult and a CloseResult with every §3 field, each exiting 0, 3 or 2 per §3" is only decidable once these per-exit field values are fixed.
objections.evidence: DONE item "`faff run open --json` prints an OpenResult and `faff run close --json` a CloseResult with every §3 field, each exiting 0, 3 or 2 per §3" against the §3 RECORD definitions and the exit-code table.
objections.predicted_consequence: two builders pass every listed test yet emit different JSON for the same refusal (one with `run_dir` set, one without), and a reviewer cannot adjudicate which is correct — the "every field" AC is undecidable for the 2 and refusal-3 exits.
objections.disposition_rationale: --json field values are defined for every exit of both verbs.
